osps_ac_01_01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default. The repository baseline script sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege and review routing goes through CODEOWNERS to the `owners` team; the settings are code, applied and drift-checked by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_03_01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
osps_br_01_01_justification: Untrusted workflow metadata is validated before use: the shared workflows accept inputs against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the pinned publish stub shape checked by lint:release-stub), and zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns where untrusted context would reach a shell.
osps_br_01_03_justification: This is the project's central architectural rule, not an incidental setting: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may declare `id-token: write`. lint:capability-boundary enforces it in the gate and fails the build if a `workflow_call` workflow ever acquires the privileged identity, so a certificate bearing this repository's identity can never be minted by a job executing a caller's code.
osps_br_01_04_justification: Collaborator-supplied input is validated rather than trusted: workflow inputs are checked against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the release-stub shape), and zizmor fails the gate on any pattern that would interpolate untrusted context into a shell.
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release carries a unique semantic version derived from conventional commits by this tool's own `stele derive version` and minted as the tag v<major>.<minor>.<patch> by the release App; the organisation tag ruleset makes tags immutable, so an identifier is never reused. Latest at the time of writing: v0.22.1. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/tags
osps_br_02_02_justification: Verified on the published release: every asset is named for the release identifier (stele-0.22.1-linux-amd64.tar.gz and the other three platform archives, stele-0.22.1.spdx.json) and each is additionally bound by digest in checksums.txt, evidence-manifest.json and the attestations.intoto.jsonl evidence bundle, so the association survives a rename. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases/tag/v0.22.1
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, releases, documentation and issue tracker are all served by GitHub over TLS, and no plaintext URI appears in the tree.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are served from GitHub over HTTPS and authenticated beyond transport: each carries attestations.intoto.jsonl (Sigstore evidence bundle) and GitHub artifact attestations covering every asset by digest, and the release tag itself is a gitsign-signed tag object. `stele verify release` checks the bundle against a pinned signer identity, fail-closed; docs/adoption.md points a first-time user at that walk before first use. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases/tag/v0.22.1
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md is generated by `stele derive notes` from conventional commits and the same section is the GitHub release body (v0.22.1's body lists its Fixed and Testing entries, each linking its pull request), so functional and security modifications are recorded per release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised: mise with an exact-version config and a lockfile carrying per-platform checksums for tools, and the language-native managers (cargo, npm) for consuming repositories. Preference is for aqua-backed tools so downloads carry checksums and attestations rather than running install scripts.
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every release ships a signature and a manifest of its assets: attestations.intoto.jsonl (Sigstore keyless, Rekor-logged), evidence-manifest.json and checksums.txt, covering the four platform archives and the SBOM by digest. The publish run verifies the published release before it completes (v0.22.1: job 'Assemble and sign Go binaries VSA / Verify the release (verdict)', success). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases/tag/v0.22.1
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md documents basic usage (the verb table and day-one `stele level --repo you/yours`) and docs/adoption.md is the full guide for a repository adopting stele without the organisation behind it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/adoption.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: docs/runbook.md has a section written from the consumer's position — 'Verifying as a consumer would' — giving the commands to check a release's attestations and Sigstore evidence bundle against the published digests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The same documentation covers authorship identity, which in a keyless design is the workflow identity: verification checks the signer's workflow ref in the certificate rather than a personal key, and the release tooling exposes an explicit signer-workflow flag so a consumer can assert which identity must have signed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Supported versions and end of life' states the scope and duration of support: only the latest release of each project receives security updates, fixes ship by rolling forward from main rather than by backporting, and a release is therefore supported exactly until the next release exists. There are no long-term support branches and no announced support windows. A repository with different needs states its own policy in its own SECURITY.md, which then replaces this one for that repository. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: The same section states when a release stops receiving security updates: a release is end-of-life for security purposes at the point the next release exists, since fixes ship only by rolling forward from main. This is a deliberate consequence of the release design - every release stays reproducible and its evidence permanent, but maintenance effort goes to the tip. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md give the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings every required tool at its pinned version from the lockfile, and `mise run ci` then runs exactly what CI runs. There are no separate libraries, frameworks or SDKs to install. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the responsibilities of each, and it is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file so it applies to every repository that does not carry its own. Who holds the maintainer role is explicit: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests are open for public discussion of proposed changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_02_justification: Released assets carry the same Apache-2.0 licence as the source; there is no separate licence for releases. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt, the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the project compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Released assets are built from this repository, which carries LICENSE at its root and LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt, with the tree-wide declaration in REUSE.toml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: go.mod lists every direct module dependency at an exact version and go.sum records their checksums; mise.toml pins the toolchain with per-platform checksums in mise.lock. Renovate reads both natively. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/go.mod
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release ships an SPDX SBOM as a release asset - verified on v0.22.1: stele-0.22.1.spdx.json beside the four platform archives, checksums.txt, evidence-manifest.json and attestations.intoto.jsonl. It is derived from the shipped binaries' embedded build information (docs/binary-sbom.md), not hand-maintained. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases/tag/v0.22.1
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organisation's repositories and their status are documented rather than assumed: docs/migration-playbook.md records which codebases join the governance and how, and the scheduled audit enumerates the live repository population from the GitHub API rather than from a hand-kept list. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/migration-playbook.md
osps_qa_04_02_justification: A release of this project comprises this single source repository; there are no subprojects releasing alongside it. Other repositories in the organisation consume this one's governance, which is by construction as strict or stricter.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed: the repository is Go source, tests, workflow YAML and documentation, and binaries exist only as release assets built by the publish workflow.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed — every tracked file is text and reviewable in a diff.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full automated suite - `mise run ci`, the org belt plus this repository's test and build tasks - on every pull request before it can be accepted, as a required check. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: Documented in both places a reader would look: README.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs, and CONTRIBUTING.md makes a green gate a requirement for every change. When they run is equally explicit — on every pull request and every push to main, with the network-bound checks on a Monday schedule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions', is the policy and it sits in the contributor-facing documentation: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, or a lint, audit task or workflow assertion where the product is configuration and policy - and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: README.md and CLAUDE.md describe the actors and actions: four verbs and `level`, each with what it owns, and the boundary that workflows orchestrate, the platform signs and stele only computes and checks. docs/ specifies every document passed between them (policies, chain notes, reports, release plans), and the organisation's docs/release.md specifies the release pipeline that runs this binary. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The external interface is the command line and the documents it consumes and emits: MAINTENANCE.md lists every verb and mode (tested against the binary's dispatch), `stele help` gives the flags, and docs/policy-schema.md, docs/assert-policy-schema.md, docs/report-schema.md and docs/chain-format.md specify the formats. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerability data is published rather than held privately: resolved reports would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on the repository, and the dependency track already publishes machine-readable VEX decisions keyed by package and version for the advisories that touch this project's dependencies. No vulnerability in this project's own code has been discovered to date. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Exactly this: the dependency track emits VEX documents keyed by package@version recording non-exploitability decisions for advisories that do not affect the project, with coverage derived rather than asserted, and the release path refuses to publish while an advisory in the SBOM is undecided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The organisation's policy (docs/dependency-track.md) is that every advisory exits through an explicit decision. For this Go repository the threshold is zero reachable advisories: govulncheck (audit:go-vulns) fails the scheduled audit on any called vulnerable symbol, and dependency-review fails a pull request that introduces a dependency with a known advisory of high or critical severity (fail-on-severity: high). https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically: dependency-review runs on every pull request (.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml, failing on high severity), govulncheck runs in the Monday audit, and Renovate raises updates as advisories land (e.g. #281, #332). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Static analysis policy' defines the remediation threshold, and it is zero: any SAST finding - CodeQL, the lint belt, zizmor and peers - fails the CI gate, and a red gate cannot merge, so findings are remediated or explicitly and reviewably suppressed with a written reason before the change lands. There is no severity triage queue for static findings because there is no state in which one is outstanding on a default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: Every change is automatically evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and trivy run in the gate, which is a required status check that a pull request cannot merge past. The requirement that the gate pass is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md; what is missing is only a stated severity threshold, recorded honestly under osps_vm_06_01. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md are the written assurance case, and docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md assess each claim against its evidence: the threat model (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, tampered artifacts), the countermeasures (the capability boundary, SHA pinning with checksums and attestations, keyless signing with transparency-log evidence), and an explicit record of what is NOT claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the org gate (`ci / ci`, a required check) on every pull request (opened, synchronize, reopened, edited), every push to main and every merge-queue group; it runs `mise run ci`, which includes this repository's `test` task (go test -race ./...) and the coverage ratchet. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: The build is the standard Go toolchain (`go build`), pinned in mise.toml (go = 1.27.4) and installed with `mise install`; no custom build tooling is involved. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/mise.toml
build_floss_tools_justification: The build uses only FLOSS tools: the Go toolchain (BSD-3-Clause), installed by mise.
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no recursive build: one `go build ./...` invocation, with the Go toolchain resolving the whole package graph itself.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Debug information is preserved: neither `mise run build` nor the release build passes -ldflags '-s -w', so DWARF and the symbol table remain; -trimpath only replaces machine paths for reproducibility. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/mise.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Building is hermetic by construction (CGO_ENABLED=0, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, -trimpath, modules pinned by go.sum) and repeatability is checked on every release, not asserted: the go-binary class builds every platform twice independently and the repro gate compares the outputs bit for bit before anything is signed. v0.22.1: 'Rebuild Go binaries (repro)' for linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-amd64 and darwin-arm64, then 'Repro gate', all success. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/actions/runs/43729938295
build_reproducible_justification: Reproducible and proven per release: the publish workflow rebuilds all four platform binaries in an independent job and the repro gate requires a bit-for-bit match before signing, attaching or publishing - a mismatch fails the release. Verified on v0.22.1's publish run ('Repro gate', success). The inputs are pinned (go.sum, go = 1.27.4, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, -trimpath). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/actions/runs/43729938295
build_standard_variables_justification: The build system is the Go toolchain's own `go build`, which reads its standard variables from the environment (GOFLAGS, CC, CGO_CFLAGS, CGO_LDFLAGS); there is no Makefile or wrapper that rewrites them. Disclosed for completeness: the `mise run build`/`test` convenience tasks set GOFLAGS=-trimpath and the repository env sets CGO_ENABLED=0, deliberately, for the hermetic release build; a packager supplying their own flags invokes `go build` directly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/mise.toml
build_justification: stele is a Go program and is built with the standard toolchain: `mise run build` (go build ./...) from a checkout, `go install github.com/monumental-archive/stele/cmd/stele@<tag>`, or the per-platform release archives built by the publish workflow. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/mise.toml
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, in the standard location, and served as the organisation default to every repository in the org. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate: golangci-lint, actionlint, zizmor, rumdl, typos and committed all run in `mise run ci` on every pull request, and a finding fails the build. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
coding_standards_justification: The coding standard is executable and language-specific: golangci-lint at `default: all` for Go, with every disabled rule justified in .golangci.yml; gofumpt and gci formatting; actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML; rumdl for Markdown; typos for spelling; Conventional Commits with a 72-column subject ceiling (committed.toml). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement through REUSE.toml's aggregate annotation rather than an inline header (per-file headers are refused by design); `reuse lint` reports 312 of 312 files with copyright information (2026-11-15), and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Signature algorithms follow whatever the Sigstore trusted root and certificates name (sigstore-go), but stele's own formats fix the digest: the chain note format links predecessors by `noteSha256` (docs/chain-format.md), so switching away from SHA-256 needs a format change, which pre-v1 is permitted but has not been made. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/chain-format.md
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic primitives are never reimplemented: stele calls Go's standard crypto packages, sigstore-go for Sigstore bundles and the trusted root, and digitorus/pkcs7 for CMS signature verification; its own code only extracts and binds the byte-exact pieces those libraries verify (internal/trust). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/internal/trust/cms.go
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is never disabled: every HTTPS client is Go's net/http with the default crypto/tls configuration, and the tree contains no tls.Config and no InsecureSkipVerify (git grep, zero hits in non-test code). Sigstore certificate chains are verified against the trusted root sigstore-go pins (docs/trusted-root.md). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/trusted-root.md
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software stores no authentication credentials or private keys at all. Secrets live in GitHub environment and organisation secrets, never in files in the repository, and release signing uses ephemeral keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is implementable with FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git are open source.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no keylengths. Release signing uses ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: stele implements no key agreement protocol: it is a command-line client whose TLS is Go's standard library.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Where it relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, SHA-256 checksums and OpenPGP-free keyless signing.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; release signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_tls12_justification: stele configures no TLS version itself (no tls.Config anywhere in the tree), so every connection uses Go's crypto/tls client default, whose minimum is TLS 1.2 (built with go 1.27.4).
crypto_used_network_justification: Every endpoint the tool contacts by itself is HTTPS: api.github.com and github.com (internal/gh/gh.go, internal/ghstore/ghstore.go) and proxy.golang.org (internal/pkgtime/pkgtime.go); no plaintext protocol is used. Disclosed: `derive facts --server-url` takes the forge URL a caller names and does not refuse an http:// scheme (see crypto_verification_private). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/internal/gh/gh.go
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Partly. Every built-in endpoint is HTTPS with default certificate verification, so the GitHub token (sent as an Authorization header) only travels after TLS verification there. But `stele derive facts --server-url` builds its client from whatever URL the caller names (gh.NewForServer) without refusing a non-https scheme, so an http:// forge URL would carry the token in clear. Recorded as Unmet until the scheme is refused. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/internal/gh/gh.go
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Integrity everywhere is SHA-256 — per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects — and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. No MD5 or SHA-1 is relied on as a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: artifact integrity uses SHA-256 (per-platform checksums in mise.lock, image digests, attestation subjects) and signing uses Sigstore's ECDSA P-256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Everything is delivered over HTTPS by GitHub. Beyond transport, the toolbelt pins every tool by exact version with per-platform checksums in mise.lock and verifies GitHub attestations, and every uses: is pinned to a full commit SHA.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are not fetched over http at use time: they are committed in mise.lock in this repository and travel with the source, and releases additionally carry Sigstore evidence bundles.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Continuously and with evidence of it working: Renovate (renovate.json) opens dependency and security updates (CHANGELOG entries marked [security], e.g. #281 for CVE-2026-84304), dependency-review.yml runs on every pull request, and the Monday audit runs govulncheck (audit:go-vulns). That scan reported reachable stdlib advisories on go 1.26.6 in late October and #332 cleared them by moving to go 1.27.4; govulncheck reports no vulnerabilities on main as of 2026-11-15. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/audit.yml
description_good_justification: The README's first paragraph states what stele is - a universal SLSA evidence engine and verifier, and the release engine that produces the evidence - followed by a table of its four verbs and `level` and what each owns. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, individually addressable by URL, open to new participants and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page carries a derived badge block: CI, OpenSSF Scorecard, the three SLSA track levels (each linked to its report), REUSE compliance, licence, codecov coverage, the Zenodo DOI and the latest release. It is rendered by `fix:badges` and a gate lint fails if it drifts. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: README.md describes the architecture as four verbs and a judge (derive, assert, emit, verify, level), what each owns and the capability boundary (stele computes and checks; workflows orchestrate; the platform signs). CLAUDE.md records the internal layout (one population enumeration in internal/population, one workflow reader in internal/workflow, strict decoding in internal/jsonx) and docs/ specifies each format. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md (what it is, day-one use, building) plus docs/: adoption.md is the front door for a new user, and policy-schema.md, assert-policy-schema.md, chain-format.md, report-schema.md, level.md, vex-join.md, trusted-root.md, versioning.md and binary-sbom.md specify each mechanism. `stele help` carries the flag reference. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/adoption.md
documentation_current_justification: Kept current by tests, not by care: the policy examples in docs/adoption.md and docs/policy-schema.md are executed by the test suite (internal/policy/doc_test.go, schema_doc_test.go), and MAINTENANCE.md's command tables are checked against the binary's own dispatch and `stele help` by internal/cli/surface_test.go, so documentation that drifts from behaviour fails the build. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the command line and the documents it reads and writes. MAINTENANCE.md lists every verb and mode (tested against the binary), `stele help` gives the flags, and docs/policy-schema.md, docs/assert-policy-schema.md, docs/report-schema.md and docs/chain-format.md specify the input policies and output formats. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md 'Why a stranger would run it' and docs/adoption.md 'Day one: zero configuration' give the quick start: install the binary, then `stele level --repo you/yours` - no clone, policy or configuration needed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/adoption.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/direction.md is the roadmap and it is unusually explicit about what the project will NOT do: a target table naming the level intended on each SLSA track, the claims policy, and the ceilings and why each sits where it does (BuildEnv is L0 by attribution, not by choice: its controls are built, but the signed build-image provenance that would make them a level belongs to producers who do not emit it; Gold-level criteria are not claimed while there is one maintainer). Open items are tracked as issues and the table is the first thing a closing issue updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md (the organisation's, served to this repository as a default community health file) states the reporting channel, 14-day acknowledgement and support policy; README.md states the security boundary (stele holds no key, mints no certificate and never runs caller code); docs/trusted-root.md states the trust anchor; docs/level.md states what a level claim does and does not establish. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/trusted-root.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Go's run-time safety checks (bounds, nil dereference, type assertions) are always on and cannot be compiled out, so every fuzz and test run has them. On top of that, the scheduled audit:go-fuzz runs every target a second time under the race detector, and the test task itself runs with -race. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/actions/runs/42644143684
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: audit:go-fuzz fails the scheduled audit on any crash, so a finding cannot sit unseen; the most recent run reports '8 target(s) ran 60s clean' and no dynamic-analysis finding is open. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/actions/runs/42644143684
dynamic_analysis_justification: Go native fuzzing over the input parsers: eight targets (FuzzParse for conventional commits, FuzzLoad for policies, FuzzLoadRoot and FuzzLoadBundle for trust material, FuzzDecodeBase64 for DSSE, FuzzLoadPolicy and FuzzSubjectDigests for assert, FuzzParseDebt for reports). The gate's lint:go-fuzz-seeds proves each builds and its seeds pass; the Monday audit's audit:go-fuzz runs each for 60s plain and 60s under the race detector. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/actions/runs/42644143684
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe language is used: stele is Go, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no C), and imports no `unsafe` package (git grep, zero hits).
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English (en-US in code and identifiers, en-GB in prose, a convention recorded in CLAUDE.md).
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are filed as issues, triaged, and either scheduled with a linked pull request or closed with the reason recorded; none are left unanswered.
external_dependencies_justification: Machine-readable and pinned: go.mod lists every module dependency and go.sum fixes their bytes; mise.toml pins the toolchain (go = 1.27.4, govulncheck) with per-platform checksums in mise.lock; renovate.json drives updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/go.mod
floss_license_justification: Released under Apache-2.0, a FLOSS licence: LICENSE at the repository root, full text in LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt, declared for every file through REUSE.toml and checked in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository and is served with hardening headers - verified against the live URL on 2026-11-15: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains; preload, content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; ..., x-frame-options: deny, x-content-type-options: nosniff. Releases are served from the same origin. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele
hardening_justification: Memory-safe Go built as static binaries with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no C toolchain in the product), GOTOOLCHAIN=local and -trimpath; golangci-lint at default: all (gosec and staticcheck included) and govulncheck; every workflow declares least-privilege permissions and pins `uses:` to full commit SHAs; releases are signed keylessly, so no signing key exists; and the tool itself holds no key and never runs caller code. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: Fail-safe defaults and complete mediation are the design: verification is fail-closed against a pinned signer identity, and a check that cannot judge reports CANNOT_JUDGE (exit 4) rather than passing; every evidence document is decoded strictly through internal/jsonx (unknown fields rejected, absent distinguished from zero); least privilege in the capability boundary (stele holds no key, mints no certificate, never runs caller code); and economy of mechanism by sharing definitions between legs (one chain.SHA256Hex for emit and verify). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
input_validation_justification: Untrusted input is checked, not trusted: every evidence and policy document is decoded strictly through internal/jsonx (unknown fields rejected, absent distinguished from zero, nil rejected explicitly), policies pass policy.Load's validation, signatures are verified before content is used, and the parsers for untrusted bytes are fuzzed (see dynamic_analysis). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
installation_common_justification: Two conventional routes: download the per-platform release archive (attested, with checksums.txt), or `go install github.com/monumental-archive/stele/cmd/stele@<tag>`, both documented in docs/adoption.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/adoption.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: README.md 'Building': `mise trust && mise install && mise run hooks:install` installs the pinned toolchain and hooks, and `mise run ci` runs exactly what CI runs. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is `go install`, which honours the standard GOBIN/GOPATH conventions for where the binary is written, or extracting a release archive wherever the user chooses; nothing is installed to a fixed path.
interact_justification: The README says what stele does, how to run it on day one and how to build it, and links the release and docs/adoption.md (how to obtain it); how to contribute, get help and report vulnerabilities is in the organisation's CONTRIBUTING.md, SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md, which GitHub serves on this repository as default community health files. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are held current by Renovate, and staticcheck (part of golangci-lint at default: all) reports use of deprecated APIs as a gate failure; actionlint does the same for workflow features. The toolchain is current (go 1.27.4). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
internationalization_justification: stele is a command-line tool whose output is machine-readable documents and operator diagnostics; it has no end-user interface strings to localise.
know_common_errors_justification: The documented threat reasoning covers the error classes specific to this software: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (enforced by zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every uses: pinned to a full commit SHA with checksums and attestations), and secret exposure in logs. See docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/build-assessment.md.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer designed and documented the project's security architecture: least privilege in workflows, an explicit capability boundary forbidding id-token: write in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency track conformance with written assurance in docs/slsa-reference.md and docs/release.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt in the REUSE-standard location; api.reuse.software reports the project REUSE-compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (Apache-2.0) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt; `reuse lint` reports 312 of 312 files with licence information (2026-11-15). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: releases are cut continuously from conventional commits, Renovate and Dependabot keep pins current, and a scheduled Monday audit re-checks settings drift, link liveness and badge truth.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Consumers pin a release by tag and move at their own pace; MAINTENANCE.md defines the versioned surface - the command surface, tested against the binary - and what a release may change. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Measured on 2026-11-15 over the repository's whole history (it began 2026-08-15, inside the six-month window): 28 of the 30 non-dependency `fix` commits on main changed a _test.go file (93%). The two without are a toolchain bump (#51) and a workflow trigger correction (#43). Renovate's 30 fix(deps) version bumps are excluded as they fix no defect in this code. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/commits/main
release_notes_justification: Every release carries notes generated by `stele derive notes` from conventional commits: CHANGELOG.md and the GitHub release body (v0.22.1: three Fixed entries and one Testing entry, each linking its pull request). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: Security fixes are marked in the notes and identified through the linked pull request: dependency fixes carry a [security] tag and link the PR that names the advisory - e.g. #281 (CVE-2026-84304, GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc) and #332 (CVE-2026-97054, GO-2026-6859). No vulnerability in stele's own code has been reported. Identifiers are reached through the link rather than repeated inline. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public, archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted through GitHub Issues; the organisation's issue forms and SUPPORT.md are served to this repository as default community health files. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues
report_responses_justification: Every issue filed in the last 12 months has been acknowledged and triaged by the maintainer; the tracker carries no unanswered reports.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. Who holds the maintainer role is unambiguous: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to in every repository, and joining that team is what becoming a maintainer concretely means. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews written against this project's own security requirements and boundary, control by control, and docs/slsa-reference.md records what is claimed and what is deliberately not. They are current, not historical: the scheduled audit re-checks the claims they rest on. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
signed_releases_justification: Verified against the published release: v0.22.1 carries attestations.intoto.jsonl (the Sigstore evidence bundle) with checksums.txt and evidence-manifest.json over the four platform archives and the SPDX SBOM. Signing is keyless - Fulcio certificate, Rekor entry, no long-lived key - and each release is built and attested by the previous stele release (N-1). `stele verify release` is the consumer's verification. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases/tag/v0.22.1
sites_https_justification: The repository, its releases and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: No open issue in this repository is labelled 'good first issue' (checked 2026-11-15: 0 of 11 open issues), so small tasks for newcomers are not currently identified. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/issues
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: gosec (enabled through golangci-lint's default: all) looks for common Go vulnerability patterns, CodeQL's security queries run for Go, govulncheck reports reachable known vulnerabilities, and zizmor covers workflow-specific ones such as template injection. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge — the gate blocks the pull request, so no finding of medium or higher severity has ever reached main unaddressed.
static_analysis_justification: golangci-lint at `default: all` (go vet, staticcheck, gosec and the rest) runs in the gate on every pull request, CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and actionlint and zizmor cover the workflows - all before any release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, and a scheduled Monday audit re-runs the network-dependent checks.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is not measured. Go's coverage tool counts statements (basic blocks), not branch outcomes, and this project does not run a separate branch-coverage tool; the 95.8% statement figure (see test_statement_coverage90) is not a branch figure and is not offered as one.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full gate, tests included, on every pull request, push to main and merge-queue group, as a required check. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `mise run ci` runs the whole gate, identically locally and in CI; `mise run test` (go test -race ./...) or plain `go test ./...` runs the suite alone. Documented in README.md 'Building'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
test_most_justification: Measured on 2026-11-15: 95.8% statement coverage across all packages (`go test -coverpkg=./... ./...`), matching the record in .coverage-floor (measured 95.8 at v0.22.1). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (the organisation's, served to this repository), item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions': a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the test that fails without it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced it. CLAUDE.md adds this repository's rule: every guard branch gets a table test. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: 95.8% statement coverage, measured on 2026-11-15 with `go test -coverpkg=./... ./...` over every package. The gate's coverage:check enforces a derived floor (.coverage-floor: 93.8, re-derived at each release as measured - 2 and only rising), and codecov renders the figure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_statement_coverage90_justification: 95.8% statement coverage, measured on 2026-11-15 with `go test -coverpkg=./... ./...`; the release machinery recorded the same 95.8 at v0.22.1 and set the floor coverage:check enforces to 93.8, which only rises. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_justification: A FLOSS automated suite in Go's standard testing package: 1127 test functions across 41 packages plus eight fuzz targets, run with `mise run test` (go test -race ./...) and in every gate run; documented in README.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/README.md
tests_are_added_justification: Measured on 2026-11-15: 57 of the 61 `feat` commits on main changed a _test.go file, including the most recent major additions (#331, #333, #334, #336). https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the documented instructions for change proposals themselves: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' - a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are Go modules identified by exact version in go.mod and fixed by go.sum, deliberately not vendored (CLAUDE.md records why), so an update is a one-line change that Renovate raises as a pull request and the gate verifies. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/go.mod
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, derived from conventional commits by `stele derive version`; docs/versioning.md and MAINTENANCE.md define what counts as breaking for this tool. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/docs/versioning.md
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated tag objects carrying a gitsign (Sigstore keyless) signature - checked on v0.22.1: the tag object holds a PKCS#7 signed message, tagger tag-mint[bot]. GitHub reports reason 'no_user' because a keyless workflow identity is not a GitHub account, not because the signature is absent. `stele assert` checks the tagger role and signature on the org's tags. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/tags
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified by an immutable v* git tag minted by the release App. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version, tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch>; the organisation tag ruleset keeps tags immutable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/releases
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are identified; dependency updates are automated and the release gate blocks on the dependency checks.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity. Renovate and Dependabot open updates continuously, trivy runs in the gate, and the dependency track records VEX decisions keyed by package and version.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters who do not request anonymity.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The gate is red on any lint finding and nothing merges red, so warnings are fixed as they appear; a suppression needs a `//nolint` naming the linter and a reason, which nolintlint enforces. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
warnings_justification: golangci-lint runs at `default: all` (go vet, staticcheck, gosec and the rest) in the gate, alongside the belt's actionlint, zizmor, typos and rumdl; any finding fails the build. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict: golangci-lint at `default: all`, where each disabled linter carries a written reason about the rule itself (one winner per rule family, or the rule contradicting the language), and nolintlint holds line-level suppressions to the same law. https://github.com/monumental-archive/stele/blob/main/.golangci.yml
